newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African business confidence seen falling further.
newsitem.headline: S.African business confidence seen falling further.

text.p: Business confidence in South Africa is set to fall over the next few months as the country adjusts to slower economic growth, the South African Chamber of Business (SACOB) said on Tuesday.
"We are now in the process of declining business confidence because of the fact that the business cycle has taken a turn for the worse," said Ben van Rensburg, SACOB director of economic policy.
Earlier SACOB said its business confidence index fell in September to 115.9 -- the lowest level in a year -- from 117.0 in August.

"The weakening in the business mood is not unexpected.... the business mood is adjusting to a more realistic assessment of the economic outlook. In addition the crime factor remains a negative element in business perceptions," SACOB said.
The organisation said the index had been hit by inflation worries, lower retail sales data, a lower bullion price, a decrease in merchandise imports and exports and lower car sales.
On the positive side a firmer rand, lower short-term interest rates, a decline in unemployment and a rising stock exchange had all boosted confidence.
Van Rensburg said South Africa's outlook was no worse than many other countries.
"Economic conditions are perceived to be worsening all over the world...we mirror what is happening in the rest of the world. We cannot isolate ourselves," he said.
Despite the setback to confidence, SACOB expected economic growth this year of three percent or more.

SACOB urged the government to push on with key aspects of its macro-economic plan, such as privatisation. The plan aims at six percent annual growth and the creation of 400,000 new jobs a year by 2000.
Van Rensburg said it was dangerous to try and judge the success of the plan at this stage and the strategy should be given two to three years to work.
"We are talking about a process, not a miracle," he said.
